Note::quote¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::quote() const

Wrap Every Cell In Double Quotes¶

quote() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with each cell wrapped in a leading and trailing ". Use it to render text for a context that expects quoted tokens — a CSV field that may contain spaces, a generated argument list, a display column where the boundaries of each value should be visible, or a log line where trailing whitespace would otherwise be invisible.

The wrap is literal and minimal: exactly one " is prepended and one appended, and the cell content in between is copied verbatim. quote() does not escape interior " characters, does not add a \ before anything, and does not skip cells that are already quoted. So quote() applied to a"b produces "a"b" — three quote characters, which is not a well-formed quoted literal. If the content can contain ", escape or replace it first (for example replace " with \"), or use a real serializer.

unquote() is the inverse: it strips one matching pair of leading/trailing " or '. Because neither method escapes, quote().unquote() round-trips exactly only when the original content has no delimiter quotes of its own.

The operation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note. An empty cell becomes "" (two bytes).

Example 1: A One-Dimensional Batch¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"payload", "two words", ""}).quote())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["\"payload\"", "\"two words\"", "\"\""]

print shows the added quotes as escaped \" inside its own quoting; the cells actually hold "payload", "two words", and "".

Example 2: A Scalar¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::make_note("solo").quote();
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"\"solo\""

The cell holds the five characters "solo".

Example 3: Shape Is Preserved¶

pluss::note::print(std::cout,
                   pluss::make_note({{"a", "b"}, {"c", "d"}}).quote())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["\"a\"", "\"b\""], 
  ["\"c\"", "\"d\""]
]

Example 4: Interior Quotes Are Not Escaped¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::make_note({"a\"b"}).quote()) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["\"a\"b\""]

The cell now holds "a"b" — a bare wrap, not a valid quoted string. Replace or escape interior " first if that matters.

Example 5: Round-Trip With unquote¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"payload", "  spaced  "}).quote().unquote())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["payload", "  spaced  "]

unquote() removes exactly the pair quote() added, so the boundary spaces in the second cell survive intact.

See Also¶

  • pluss::coden::Note::unquote: strip one matching pair of leading/trailing " or '.

  • pluss::coden::Note::surround: wrap each cell in an arbitrary prefix/suffix pair rather than double quotes.

  • Note::replace: escape interior " before quoting when the result must be a valid literal.
